transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess things have been harder since my sister and her baby moved back home. I’ve been more on edge and kind of down, snapping at people over little stuff. Then I’m already drained when I get to class or the shop. I’m still managing, mostly, but I missed a couple deadlines and backed out of helping with the theater set because I couldn’t keep everything straight.
When exactly did you start noticing these feelings of being on edge and down—was it right around the time your sister and her baby moved back in, or did it start earlier or later than that?
I was doing okay before they moved in. Then, within a couple weeks of the house getting crowded, I started feeling more on edge and down.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you'd normally enjoy since this all started?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear loss of interest in things I normally like.
Is your worrying mostly about the situation at home with your sister and the baby, or do you find yourself worrying a lot about other things too, like school, work, or health, even unrelated to that?
Mostly it’s about home—my sister and the baby being there and everything feeling crowded. That’s what gets me worked up, and then I’m already drained when I get to class or the shop.
Besides feeling on edge and snapping at people, have you done things like breaking rules, skipping responsibilities on purpose, or acting out in ways that got you in trouble at home, school, or work?
No, I haven’t really been doing anything like that. I’ve been irritable, but I haven’t gotten in trouble or purposely skipped things or broken rules.
Besides feeling on edge, have you noticed feeling sad, hopeless, or tearful much of the time since this started?
Yeah, I’ve been feeling more down than usual since they moved in. Not hopeless exactly, but just worn out and kind of low a lot of the time.

Symptoms are directly tied to this stressor, causing functional impairment (missed deadlines, withdrawal from activities) but do not meet full criteria for major depressive disorder (no anhedonia, no hopelessness) or generalized anxiety disorder (worry is situational, not pervasive across multiple domains).
